Name: Domainsdb.info__2
Description: Registered Domain Names Search
Introduction: The Domainsdb.info API is a powerful tool used to easily search for registered domain names. Through this API, users can access the following functions: 1) Search for registered domain names by keyword or phrase. 2) Retrieve details on domain name ownership, including registrant information, the domain's status, and creation and expiration dates. 3) Analyze domain name statistics, including global usage and distribution. With this API, developers can easily integrate domain search functionality into their applications.
Functions:
1. Name: searchDomains
Description: This function allows users to search for registered domain names by keyword or phrase.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- query: String. The keyword or phrase to search for.
- tld: String. The top-level domain to search within. If not specified, all TLDs will be searched.
Output: An array of JSON objects, each representing a registered domain name that matches the search query. Each object contains the following keys:
- domainName: String. The registered domain name.
- createDt: String. The date the domain was created.
- updateDt: String. The date the domain was last updated.
- expireDt: String. The date the domain will expire.
- registrarName: String. The name of the domain's registrar.
- registrantName: String. The name of the domain's registrant.
- registrantEmail: String. The email address of the domain's registrant.
- registrantOrganization: String. The organization of the domain's registrant.
- status: String. The status of the domain (e.g. active, inactive, pending, etc.).

2. Name: getDomainDetails
Description: This function allows users to retrieve details on domain name ownership, including registrant information, the domain's status, and creation and expiration dates.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following key:
- domainName: String. The registered domain name to retrieve details for.
Output: A JSON object representing the domain's details. The object contains the following keys:
- domainName: String. The registered domain name.
- createDt: String. The date the domain was created.
- updateDt: String. The date the domain was last updated.
- expireDt: String. The date the domain will expire.
- registrarName: String. The name of the domain's registrar.
- registrantName: String. The name of the domain's registrant.
- registrantEmail: String. The email address of the domain's registrant.
- registrantOrganization: String. The organization of the domain's registrant.
- status: String. The status of the domain (e.g. active, inactive, pending, etc.).

3. Name: getDomainStats
Description: This function allows users to analyze domain name statistics, including global usage and distribution.
Input: Optional. JSON object with the following keys:
- tld: String. The top-level domain to retrieve statistics for. If not specified, statistics for all TLDs will be returned.
Output: A JSON object representing the domain statistics. The object contains the following keys:
- totalDomains: Integer. The total number of registered domains.
- tldCount: Integer. The number of registered domains for the specified TLD (if specified).
- tldPercentage: Float. The percentage of registered domains for the specified TLD (if specified).
- topCountries: Array of JSON objects. Each object represents a country and contains the following keys:
  - countryCode: String. The ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code.
  - countryName: String. The name of the country.
  - domainCount: Integer. The number of registered domains for the country.
  - domainPercentage: Float. The percentage of registered domains for the country.

Name: Feedbin
Description: RSS reader
Introduction: The Feedbin API is a powerful tool that allows developers to integrate Feedbin's RSS reader functionality into their own applications. This API provides the following functions: 1) Get all of a user's feeds. 2) Get all of a user's unread entries. 3) Retrieve entries from a specified feed by timestamp. 4) Star, mark as read, or un-mark as read an entry. 5) Retrieve metadata about a feed, including its title, URL, and icon. With these functions, developers can create innovative, user-friendly applications that streamline the RSS reading experience.
Functions:
1. Name: getUserFeeds
Description: Retrieves all of a user's feeds.
Input: None
Output: Returns an array of JSON objects, each representing a feed. Each object contains the following fields:
- id: Integer. The unique ID of the feed.
- title: String. The title of the feed.
- feed_url: String. The URL of the feed.
- site_url: String. The URL of the feed's website.
- is_spark: Boolean. Indicates whether the feed is a Spark feed.
- last_updated_at: String. The timestamp of the feed's last update.

2. Name: getUserUnreadEntries
Description: Retrieves all of a user's unread entries.
Input: None
Output: Returns an array of JSON objects, each representing an unread entry. Each object contains the following fields:
- id: Integer. The unique ID of the entry.
- title: String. The title of the entry.
- author: String. The author of the entry.
- content: String. The content of the entry.
- url: String. The URL of the entry.
- feed_id: Integer. The ID of the feed that the entry belongs to.
- published: String. The timestamp of the entry's publication.
- created_at: String. The timestamp of the entry's creation.
- updated_at: String. The timestamp of the entry's last update.

3. Name: getFeedEntriesByTimestamp
Description: Retrieves entries from a specified feed by timestamp.
Input: 
- feed_id: Required. Integer. The ID of the feed to retrieve entries from.
- timestamp: Required. String. The timestamp to retrieve entries from, in the format "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ".
Output: Returns an array of JSON objects, each representing an entry. Each object contains the following fields:
- id: Integer. The unique ID of the entry.
- title: String. The title of the entry.
- author: String. The author of the entry.
- content: String. The content of the entry.
- url: String. The URL of the entry.
- feed_id: Integer. The ID of the feed that the entry belongs to.
- published: String. The timestamp of the entry's publication.
- created_at: String. The timestamp of the entry's creation.
- updated_at: String. The timestamp of the entry's last update.

4. Name: markEntry
Description: Stars, marks as read, or un-marks as read an entry.
Input: 
- entry_id: Required. Integer. The ID of the entry to mark.
- star: Optional. Boolean. Indicates whether to star the entry.
- read: Optional. Boolean. Indicates whether to mark the entry as read.
Output: Returns a JSON object representing the updated entry. The object contains the same fields as the entry object returned by the getFeedEntriesByTimestamp function.

5. Name: getFeedMetadata
Description: Retrieves metadata about a feed, including its title, URL, and icon.
Input: 
- feed_id: Required. Integer. The ID of the feed to retrieve metadata for.
Output: Returns a JSON object representing the feed's metadata. The object contains the following fields:
- title: String. The title of the feed.
- feed_url: String. The URL of the feed.
- site_url: String. The URL of the feed's website.
- icon_url: String. The URL of the feed's icon.

Name: EPA
Description: Web services and data sets from the US Environmental Protection Agency
Introduction: The EPA (Environmental Protection Agency) provides a variety of web services and data sets through their API, available for developers to integrate into their own applications. This API contains features such as: 1) Air Quality - real-time air quality measurements from all over the United States 2) Toxics Release Inventory - information regarding industrial facilities that have reported releases of toxic chemicals 3) Enforcement and Compliance History Online - a repository of compliance and enforcement action data for EPA-regulated facilities. With this API, developers can create applications that provide users with up-to-date environmental information and data.
Functions:
1. Name: getAirQualityByZipCode
Description: Retrieves real-time air quality measurements for a specific zip code.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- zipCode: String. The zip code for which to retrieve air quality data.
Output: JSON object with the following keys:
- AQI: Integer. The Air Quality Index for the specified zip code.
- Category: String. The category of air quality (Good, Moderate, Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups, Unhealthy, Very Unhealthy, Hazardous).
- Pollutants: Array of JSON objects. Each object contains information about a specific pollutant, including its name, concentration, and category.

2. Name: getFacilitiesByLocation
Description: Retrieves information about EPA-regulated facilities within a specified radius of a location.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- latitude: Float. The latitude of the location around which to search for facilities.
- longitude: Float. The longitude of the location around which to search for facilities.
- radius: Integer. The radius (in miles) around the specified location within which to search for facilities.
Output: Array of JSON objects, each representing a facility. Each object contains the following keys:
- FacilityName: String. The name of the facility.
- Address: String. The address of the facility.
- City: String. The city in which the facility is located.
- State: String. The state in which the facility is located.
- Zip: String. The zip code of the facility.
- Latitude: Float. The latitude of the facility.
- Longitude: Float. The longitude of the facility.
- LastInspectionDate: String. The date of the facility's last inspection.
- LastInspectionType: String. The type of the facility's last inspection.
- Violations: Array of JSON objects. Each object contains information about a specific violation, including its date, type, and status.

3. Name: getToxicReleaseInventoryByChemical
Description: Retrieves information about industrial facilities that have reported releases of a specific chemical.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- chemicalName: String. The name of the chemical for which to retrieve information.
Output: Array of JSON objects, each representing a facility that has reported a release of the specified chemical. Each object contains the following keys:
- FacilityName: String. The name of the facility.
- Address: String. The address of the facility.
- City: String. The city in which the facility is located.
- State: String. The state in which the facility is located.
- Zip: String. The zip code of the facility.
- Latitude: Float. The latitude of the facility.

With its user-friendly interface, this API enables developers to quickly retrieve a variety of domain-related information, such as domain expiration data and registrar details. The API provides the following features: 1) retrieve all registered domains; 2) search for domains based on keywords; 3) retrieve domain name registration details such as creation date, expiration date, registrar name and more. Name: CircleCI
Description: Automate the software development process using continuous integration and continuous delivery
Introduction: The CircleCI API (Application Programming Interface) is a platform that allows users to automate the software development process using continuous integration and continuous delivery. It provides the following functions: 1) Create and manage projects, workflows, and builds. 2) Access build artifacts, test data, and build logs. 3) Trigger builds through webhooks and API calls. 4) Retrieve performance metrics and historical data on builds. By integrating with CircleCI, developers can increase the speed and reliability of their software delivery while reducing the risk of errors.

Input: Required. JSON object with the following fields:

- branch: String. The name of the branch to build.
Output: The function will return a JSON object with information about the triggered build, including its build number, status, and URL.

Description: This function allows users to retrieve details about a specific build, including its status, duration, and artifacts.

4. Name: Get Build Artifacts
Description: This function allows users to retrieve the artifacts generated by a specific build.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following fields:

- workflow_id: String. The ID of the workflow to retrieve details for.

- workflow_id: String. The ID of the workflow to cancel.

Description: This function allows users to retrieve a list of environments for a specific project.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following fields:
- project_slug: String. The slug of the project to retrieve environments for.

Description: This function allows users to retrieve details about a specific environment, including its variables and URL.

Name: Universalis
Description: Final Fantasy XIV market board data
Introduction: The Universalis API is an essential resource for any Final Fantasy XIV player looking to stay up-to-date on market board data. This API provides accurate price data for all items sold on the market board. It offers the following features: 1) Retrieve current market prices for an item. 2) Retrieve historical market prices for an item. 3) Search for items by their name in multiple languages. 4) Retrieve a list of users who are selling an item. Additionally, this API allows for frequent updates, making it an integral tool for helping players make informed decisions when buying and selling items on the market board.

    Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:

    Output: JSON object with the following keys:
        - world: String. The name of the world the prices are for.
        - itemID: Integer. The ID of the item the prices are for.
        - prices: JSON object with the following keys:
            - NQ: JSON object with the following keys:
                - minPrice: Integer. The minimum price for the item in NQ quality.
                - maxPrice: Integer. The maximum price for the item in NQ quality.
                - averagePrice: Integer. The average price for the item in NQ quality.
            - HQ: JSON object with the following keys:
                - minPrice: Integer. The minimum price for the item in HQ quality.
                - maxPrice: Integer. The maximum price for the item in HQ quality.
                - averagePrice: Integer. The average price for the item in HQ quality.

        - itemID: Integer. The ID of the item to retrieve prices for.
        - numDays: Integer. The number of days of historical data to retrieve.

        - world: String. The name of the world the prices are for.
        - itemID: Integer. The ID of the item the prices are for.
        - prices: JSON array of JSON objects with the following keys:

            - NQ: JSON object with the following keys:
                - minPrice: Integer. The minimum price for the item in NQ quality.
                - maxPrice: Integer. The maximum price for the item in NQ quality.
                - averagePrice: Integer. The average price for the item in NQ quality.
            - HQ: JSON object with the following keys:
                - minPrice: Integer. The minimum price for the item in HQ quality.
                - maxPrice: Integer. The maximum price for the item in HQ quality.
                - averagePrice: Integer. The average price for the item in HQ quality.

        - name: String. The name of the item in the specified language.
        - icon: String. The URL of the item's icon.

    Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:

    Output: JSON array of JSON objects with the following keys:
        - sellerID: Integer. The ID of the seller.
        - sellerName: String. The name of the seller.
        - world: String. The name of the world the seller is on.
        - pricePerUnit: Integer. The price per unit the seller is selling the item for.
        - quantity: Integer. The quantity of the item the seller is selling.

Name: Czech National Bank
Description: A collection of exchange rates
Introduction: The Czech National Bank API (Application Programming Interface) is a reliable source of daily exchange rate information provided by the Czech National Bank. This API provides the following features: 1) Retrieve the current exchange rates for selected currencies as well as historical rates that can be filtered by dates. 2) The rates are updated daily, providing accurate and reliable exchange rate information in real-time for both individuals and businesses.
Functions:
1. Name: getCurrentExchangeRates
   Description: Retrieve the current exchange rates for selected currencies.
   Input: {"currencies": "Optional. Array of strings. List of currency codes (e.g., 'USD', 'EUR') to retrieve exchange rates for. If not provided, all available currencies will be returned."}
   Output: A JSON object containing the exchange rates for the selected currencies, with each currency code as a key and its exchange rate as the value.

2. Name: getHistoricalExchangeRates
   Description: Retrieve historical exchange rates for selected currencies, filtered by date range.
   Input: {"currencies": "Optional. Array of strings. List of currency codes (e.g., 'USD', 'EUR') to retrieve exchange rates for. If not provided, all available currencies will be returned.", "startDate": "Required. String. The start date of the date range in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD'.", "endDate": "Required. String. The end date of the date range in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD'."}
   Output: A JSON object containing the historical exchange rates for the selected currencies and date range, with each currency code as a key and an array of objects containing the date and exchange rate as the value.

3. Name: searchCurrency
   Description: Search for a currency by its code or name.
   Input: {"query": "Required. String. The search query, which can be a currency code (e.g., 'USD') or a currency name (e.g., 'US Dollar')."}
   Output: A JSON object containing the currency code, currency name, and country of the matching currency.

4. Name: listAvailableCurrencies
   Description: Retrieve a list of all available currencies supported by the Czech National Bank API.
   Input: None
   Output: A JSON array containing objects with the currency code, currency name, and country for each available currency.

Name: Lexigram
Description: NLP that extracts mentions of clinical concepts from text, gives access to clinical ontology
Introduction: Lexigram is a powerful Natural Language Processing (NLP) API that helps extract mentions of clinical concepts from any type of text. This tool is primarily meant for healthcare organizations and developers looking to integrate structured clinical data into their platforms. The Lexigram API provides a set of functions including: 1) Identifying and extracting clinical mentions from text data. 2) Access to a clinical ontology containing codes and descriptions for various medical concepts. 3) A normalization feature that can convert unstructured medical data into structured, machine-readable data. Overall, the Lexigram API offers versatile and effective tools to help healthcare professionals make better use of their clinical data.
Functions:
1. Name: extractClinicalMentions
Description: Extracts clinical mentions from a given text data.
Input: {"text": "Required. String. The text data from which clinical mentions need to be extracted."}
Output: A list of clinical mentions found in the text data, including their start and end positions, and the corresponding medical concept codes and descriptions.

2. Name: searchClinicalConcepts
Description: Searches for clinical concepts based on a given query.
Input: {"query": "Required. String. The search query to find relevant clinical concepts.", "limit": "Optional. Integer. The maximum number of results to return."}
Output: A list of matching clinical concepts, including their codes, descriptions, and related medical concepts.

3. Name: getClinicalConceptDetails
Description: Retrieves detailed information about a specific clinical concept.
Input: {"conceptId": "Required. String. The unique identifier of the clinical concept."}
Output: Detailed information about the clinical concept, including its code, description, synonyms, and related medical concepts.

4. Name: normalizeClinicalData
Description: Converts unstructured medical data into structured, machine-readable data.
Input: {"text": "Required. String. The unstructured medical data that needs to be normalized."}
Output: A structured representation of the input medical data, including extracted clinical mentions, their corresponding medical concept codes and descriptions, and any additional relevant information.

5. Name: listClinicalConceptCategories
Description: Lists all available clinical concept categories.
Input: None
Output: A list of clinical concept categories, including their names, descriptions, and the number of concepts in each category.

6. Name: getClinicalConceptsByCategory
Description: Retrieves clinical concepts belonging to a specific category.
Input: {"categoryName": "Required. String. The name of the clinical concept category.", "limit": "Optional. Integer. The maximum number of results to return."}
Output: A list of clinical concepts belonging to the specified category, including their codes, descriptions, and related medical concepts.

Name: Line
Description: Line Login, Share on Line, Social Plugins and more
Introduction: The Line API is a versatile platform designed to streamline social networking for both users and developers alike. With its line login feature, users can access a wide range of social plugins and share content with their friends on Line, the popular messaging app. Additionally, the Line API offers a host of features and functionality to support developers in creating innovative, engaging user experiences. Specifically, it provides the following benefits: 1) Line login that allows users to easily access your app. 2) Share on Line button to make it easy to share content on Line. 3) Social plugins that allow developers to add interactive features to their websites. 4) Messaging API for developers to create chatbots and messaging services. With its user-friendly design and accessible features, the Line API is the perfect tool for enhancing and extending social networking capabilities.

Name: APIs.guru
Description: Wikipedia for Web APIs, OpenAPI/Swagger specs for public APIs
Introduction: The APIs.guru API is known as the Wikipedia for Web APIs that provides OpenAPI/Swagger specifications for public APIs. It aims to provide a comprehensive and up-to-date list of all the available public APIs and their associated specifications, enabling developers to access and utilize the data that they need. The API offers the following key functions: 1) Browse and explore API collections by categories or search terms. 2) Easily access accurate documentation and Swagger specifications for each API. 3) Get automated updates on any changes made to the APIs in the database. Name: arXiv
Description: Curated research-sharing platform: physics, mathematics, quantitative finance, and economics
Introduction: The arXiv API (Application Programming Interface) is a resourceful tool for researchers, students, and enthusiasts alike. Its primary purpose is to allow developers to access the wealth of information available on the arXiv platform, which is a resource for scholarly research articles in the fields of physics, mathematics, quantitative finance, and economics. The functions provided by this API include: 1) Search for research articles by a variety of fields, including author name, keyword, and publication date. 2) Retrieve metadata about a specific article, including its title, author(s), abstract, and publication date. 3) Retrieve the full text for a specific article, subject to certain usage restrictions. With these features, the arXiv API provides convenient access to vast amounts of research, promoting collaboration and innovation in scientific fields.
Functions:
1. Name: search
Description: This function allows users to search for research articles based on a variety of fields, including author name, keyword, and publication date.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- search_query: String. The search query to be used for the search.
- start: Integer. The index of the first result to be returned.
- max_results: Integer. The maximum number of results to be returned.
Output: JSON object with the following keys:
- total_results: Integer. The total number of results matching the search query.
- results: Array of JSON objects, each representing a research article. Each object has the following keys:
  - id: String. The unique identifier for the article.
  - title: String. The title of the article.
  - authors: Array of strings. The names of the authors of the article.
  - summary: String. A brief summary of the article.
  - published: String. The publication date of the article in the format "YYYY-MM-DD".
  
2. Name: retrieveMetadata
Description: This function allows users to retrieve metadata about a specific research article, including its title, author(s), abstract, and publication date.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following key:
- id: String. The unique identifier for the article.
Output: JSON object with the following keys:
- id: String. The unique identifier for the article.
- title: String. The title of the article.
- authors: Array of strings. The names of the authors of the article.
- summary: String. A brief summary of the article.
- published: String. The publication date of the article in the format "YYYY-MM-DD".

3. Name: retrieveFullText
Description: This function allows users to retrieve the full text for a specific research article, subject to certain usage restrictions.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following key:
- id: String. The unique identifier for the article.
Output: String. The full text of the article, subject to usage restrictions.

Name: Freelancer
Description: Hire freelancers to get work done
Introduction: The Freelancer API is an online platform where businesses can connect with freelancers to get their work done. With a simple integration into your application, the API provides access to a wide range of features, including: 1) Search for freelancers with the required skills. 2) Post projects and receive proposals from freelancers. 3) Management of projects and payments. 4) Get real-time notifications on project updates. Whether it's a small task or a complex project, Freelancer API is an ideal choice for businesses looking for reliable and cost-effective solutions to meet their project requirements.
Functions:
1. Name: searchFreelancers
Description: This function allows businesses to search for freelancers based on their skills and other criteria.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- keywords: String. Keywords related to the project.
- skills: String. Skills required for the project.
- country: String. Country where the freelancer is located.
- hourly_rate_min: Integer. Minimum hourly rate of the freelancer.
- hourly_rate_max: Integer. Maximum hourly rate of the freelancer.
Output: An array of JSON objects, each representing a freelancer. Each object contains the following keys:
- id: Integer. Unique identifier of the freelancer.
- username: String. Username of the freelancer.
- display_name: String. Display name of the freelancer.
- profile_picture_url: String. URL of the freelancer's profile picture.
- hourly_rate: Integer. Hourly rate of the freelancer.
- skills: Array of strings. Skills of the freelancer.
- country: String. Country where the freelancer is located.

2. Name: postProject
Description: This function allows businesses to post a project and receive proposals from freelancers.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- title: String. Title of the project.
- description: String. Description of the project.
- skills: Array of strings. Skills required for the project.
- budget: Integer. Budget for the project.
- currency: String. Currency of the budget.
- duration: Integer. Duration of the project in days.
Output: JSON object representing the posted project. The object contains the following keys:
- id: Integer. Unique identifier of the project.
- title: String. Title of the project.
- description: String. Description of the project.
- skills: Array of strings. Skills required for the project.
- budget: Integer. Budget for the project.
- currency: String. Currency of the budget.
- duration: Integer. Duration of the project in days.
- status: String. Status of the project.

3. Name: getProject
Description: This function allows businesses to retrieve information about a specific project.
Input: Required. Integer representing the project ID.
Output: JSON object representing the project. The object contains the following keys:
- id: Integer. Unique identifier of the project.
- title: String. Title of the project.
- description: String. Description of the project.
- skills: Array of strings. Skills required for the project.
- budget: Integer. Budget for the project.
- currency: String. Currency of the budget.
- duration: Integer. Duration of the project in days.
- status: String. Status of the project.

4. Name: updateProject
Description: This function allows businesses to update information about a specific project.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- id: Integer. Unique identifier of the project.
- title: String. Title of the project.
- description: String. Description of the project.
- skills: Array of strings. Skills required for the project.
- budget: Integer. Budget for the project.
- currency: String. Currency of the budget.
- duration: Integer. Duration of the project in days.
Output: JSON object representing the updated project. The object contains the same keys as the getProject function.

5. Name: getProposals
Description: This function allows businesses to retrieve proposals for a specific project.
Input: Required. Integer representing the project ID.
Output: An array of JSON objects, each representing a proposal. Each object contains the following keys:
- id: Integer. Unique identifier of the proposal.
- bidder_id: Integer. Unique identifier of the freelancer who submitted the proposal.
- bidder_username: String. Username of the freelancer who submitted the proposal.
- bid_amount: Integer. Amount proposed by the freelancer.
- bid_duration: Integer. Duration proposed by the freelancer in days.
- bid_time: String. Time when the proposal was submitted.

6. Name: acceptProposal
Description: This function allows businesses to accept a proposal for a specific project.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- id: Integer. Unique identifier of the proposal.
- project_id: Integer. Unique identifier of the project.
Output: JSON object representing the accepted proposal. The object contains the following keys:
- id: Integer. Unique identifier of the proposal.
- bidder_id: Integer. Unique identifier of the freelancer who submitted the proposal.
- bidder_username: String. Username of the freelancer who submitted the proposal.
- bid_amount: Integer. Amount proposed by the freelancer.
- bid_duration: Integer. Duration proposed by the freelancer in days.
- bid_time: String. Time when the proposal was submitted.
- status: String. Status of the proposal.

7. Name: getNotifications
Description: This function allows businesses to retrieve real-time notifications on project updates.
Input: None.
Output: An array of JSON objects, each representing a notification. Each object contains the following keys:
- id: Integer. Unique identifier of the notification.
- type: String. Type of the notification.
- message: String. Message of the notification.
- time: String. Time when the notification was sent.

Name: Vadivelu HTTP Codes
Description: On demand HTTP Codes with images
Introduction: Vadivelu HTTP Codes is a unique API that provides HTTP status codes with accompanying images of the popular Indian comedian Vadivelu. This API is a fun and creative way of presenting HTTP codes to developers and users alike. Name: Tokopedia
Description: Tokopedia's Official API for integration of various services from Tokopedia
Introduction: The Tokopedia API is a comprehensive suite of tools that enables developers to leverage Tokopedia's vast array of e-commerce capabilities in their own applications. This official API provides a wide range of services, from product searches and price comparisons to product details retrieval and order management. With low-coupling between functions, this APIs features include but are not limited to: 1) Search for products or deals on Tokopedia's platform. 2) Retrieve product details including price, availability, and ratings. 3) Manage orders for successful transactions including cancelling, refunding, and tracking orders. Tokopedia's robust API ensures that developers can build applications with powerful e-commerce functionality, making it an essential tool for anyone looking to incorporate Tokopedia's e-commerce services into their platform.
Functions:
1. Name: searchProducts
Description: This function allows users to search for products on Tokopedia's platform based on specific keywords and filters.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- q: String. The search query.
- rows: Integer. The number of results to return per page. Maximum is 50.
- start: Integer. The starting index of the results to return.
- filter: String. The filter to apply to the search results. Options include "official", "gold", "free_shipping", "wholesale", and "overseas".
Output: An array of JSON objects, each representing a product. Each object contains information such as the product ID, name, price, image URL, and seller information.

2. Name: getProductDetail
Description: This function allows users to retrieve detailed information about a specific product on Tokopedia's platform.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following key:
- id: Integer. The ID of the product to retrieve details for.
Output: A JSON object representing the product. The object contains information such as the product ID, name, price, image URLs, seller information, ratings, and reviews.

3. Name: createOrder
Description: This function allows users to create a new order for a product on Tokopedia's platform.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- product_id: Integer. The ID of the product to order.
- quantity: Integer. The quantity of the product to order.
- courier: String. The courier to use for shipping. Options include "jne", "tiki", and "pos".
- service_type: String. The type of shipping service to use. Options include "regular", "yes", and "super".
- notes: String. Any additional notes or instructions for the seller.
- buyer_name: String. The name of the buyer.
- buyer_phone: String. The phone number of the buyer.
- buyer_email: String. The email address of the buyer.
- buyer_address: String. The shipping address of the buyer.
Output: A JSON object representing the newly created order. The object contains information such as the order ID, product information, shipping information, and payment information.

4. Name: cancelOrder
Description: This function allows users to cancel an existing order on Tokopedia's platform.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following key:
- order_id: Integer. The ID of the order to cancel.
Output: A JSON object representing the cancelled order. The object contains information such as the order ID, product information, shipping information, and payment information.

5. Name: refundOrder
Description: This function allows users to request a refund for an existing order on Tokopedia's platform.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- order_id: Integer. The ID of the order to request a refund for.
- reason: String. The reason for the refund request.
- notes: String. Any additional notes or instructions for the seller.
Output: A JSON object representing the refunded order. The object contains information such as the order ID, product information, shipping information, and payment information.

6. Name: trackOrder
Description: This function allows users to track the status of an existing order on Tokopedia's platform.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following key:
- order_id: Integer. The ID of the order to track.
Output: A JSON object representing the tracked order. The object contains information such as the order ID, product information, shipping information, and payment information, as well as the current status of the order.

The API provides various functions, including: 1) Query and search for drug data, including product names, active ingredients, and adverse events reports. 2) Search recalls by product type, reason, classification level, date and other factors, and 3) search device data by device name, manufacturer and classification. With the openFDA API, users can access FDA data and resources in a flexible and easy-to-use way.

Introduction: The NetworkCalc API is a comprehensive suite of tools designed to make network calculations and analysis easier. It offers a wide range of functionalities to help network administrators and security professionals manage their network more effectively. The API includes the following functions: 1) Subnet Calculator, which helps in calculating subnets, hosts, and other network parameters. 2) DNS tools, which provide lookup and management of domain names. 3) Binary Calculator, which is used to convert binary numbers to decimal or vice versa. 4) Security tools, including hash generators, password generators and validators. With NetworkCalc API, integrating these functionalities in your apps and systems is a breeze.

These functions include: 1) Retrieving the nameday for a specific day and country. 2) Retrieving all namedays for a specific country. 3) Searching for a specific nameday by name. The API offers an easy-to-use and comprehensive way to access and integrate nameday data into various applications.

Output: A JSON object containing a list of nameday information matching the searched name, including the date, country, and the list of names celebrating their nameday on that date. The results can be filtered by country and language if specified.

Introduction: The OpenStreetMap API (Application Programming Interface) provides developers with access to a wealth of data regarding geographic locations, navigation, and more. It offers a range of functions, including: 1) Retrieving map data, including street names and locations of points of interest. 2) Geocoding, which is the process of converting street addresses to geographic coordinates. 3) Routing, which provides directions between points on the map. 4) Search for points of interest, such as restaurants or stores. With the OpenStreetMap API, developers can create powerful location-based applications and services.

Description: Retrieves map data, including street names and locations of points of interest.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- bbox: String. The bounding box of the area to retrieve data for, in the format "left,bottom,right,top".
- zoom: Integer. The zoom level of the map data to retrieve.
Output: A JSON object containing the map data for the specified area and zoom level.

2. Name: Geocoding
Description: Converts street addresses to geographic coordinates.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- q: String. The address to geocode.

3. Name: Routing
Description: Provides directions between points on the map.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- start: String. The starting point of the route, in the format "latitude,longitude".
- end: String. The ending point of the route, in the format "latitude,longitude".
Output: A JSON object containing the directions for the specified route.

4. Name: Search for Points of Interest
Description: Searches for points of interest, such as restaurants or stores.
Input: Required. JSON object with the following keys:
- q: String. The search query.
- bbox: String. The bounding box of the area to search in, in the format "left,bottom,right,top".

Introduction: Chainlink is a decentralized oracle network that allows developers to easily connect smart contracts to off-chain data, web APIs, and traditional payment systems. With this API, developers can build hybrid smart contracts that combine the security and transparency of blockchain technology with real-world data and payment systems. Some of the key features of Chainlink include: 1) Securely connect smart contracts to any API or data source. 2) Use Chainlink's decentralized oracle network to ensure data integrity and reliability. 3) Leverage Chainlink's payment capabilities to create complex financial contracts. With Chainlink, developers can build truly decentralized applications that are both secure and flexible, leveraging the full power of blockchain technology.

1) Query API - execute SQL queries and retrieve results programmatically
2) Setting API - manage Metabase settings and preferences
3) Collection API - manage collections of items like dashboards, questions, and snippets
4) User API - manage users and groups
5) Permissions API - manage permissions and access levels for users and groups
Each function has a clear and distinct purpose, allowing users to interact with Metabase in powerful and flexible ways.
